segments.t: With shell integration, the shell tells korTTY where each prompt starts, where the command you type starts, where its output starts and how the command ended. It does so with invisible OSC 133 marks, the same ones iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty and VS Code read, which a few lines in the shell's startup file add. korTTY uses them to jump between the prompts of a long session with one key, to select or copy what the last command printed, to show in the command timestamp sidebar how each command ended and how long it ran, and to tell you when a long command finishes in a tab you are not looking at. In an SSH session they also tell korTTY that the shell is at its prompt, which the AI Agent's KTPH000 commands and the question before closing a busy tab rely on.
Without the marks nothing changes: the keys reach the shell as before, and the terminal looks and behaves as it always did.
KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 on macOS, KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on Windows and Linux
KTPH000EditKTPH001 menu and the terminal's right-click menu
KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 on macOS, KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on Windows and Linux
KTPH000EditKTPH001 menu and the terminal's right-click menu
A jump scrolls the pane so that the prompt shows at the top of the view, with the command and its output below it.
At the bottom of the scrollback, KTPH000Previous PromptKTPH001 goes to the prompt of the command before the one you are typing, and each further press goes one command further back.

After you scrolled by hand, a jump starts from the top line you see: KTPH000Previous PromptKTPH001 goes to the closest prompt above it and KTPH002Next PromptKTPH003 to the closest one below it, so a prompt you can already see is not skipped.
A prompt on the last screen cannot move to the top, because the view cannot scroll past the bottom. The view then stays where it is, and the next press continues from that prompt.
KTPH000Next PromptKTPH001 after the last prompt goes back to the bottom. KTPH002Previous PromptKTPH003 above the first prompt does nothing.

The keys act in the pane that has the keyboard focus, and each pane of a split tab has its own marks. KTPH000Edit → Previous PromptKTPH001 and KTPH002Edit → Next PromptKTPH003 act in the focused pane of the selected tab, the right-click menu in the pane you right-clicked. When the KTPH004EditKTPH005 menu cannot jump, the status bar says why.

The keys are korTTY's only while the pane has prompt marks and shows its normal screen. In a pane without marks, and while a full-screen program such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002 or KTPH003 runs, they reach the program exactly as before: on Windows and Linux as KTPH004 and KTPH005. With KTPH020broadcast modeKTPH021 on, or with the pane taking part in KTPH022multi-execKTPH023, a jump acts only in the pane you pressed the key in; when the key goes to the program instead, it goes to the other panes as well on Windows and Linux, like any other arrow key. Windows Terminal and GNOME Terminal scroll by one line with KTPH024KTPH006KTPH025+KTPH026KTPH007KTPH027+KTPH028KTPH008KTPH029 and KTPH030KTPH009KTPH031+KTPH032KTPH010KTPH033+KTPH034KTPH011KTPH035; in korTTY that is KTPH036KTPH012KTPH037+KTPH038KTPH013KTPH039 and KTPH040KTPH014KTPH041+KTPH042KTPH015KTPH043 (KTPH044KTPH016KTPH045+KTPH046KTPH017KTPH047 and KTPH048KTPH018KTPH049+KTPH050KTPH019KTPH051 on macOS).

A pane with prompt marks has KTPH000Previous PromptKTPH001, KTPH002Next PromptKTPH003, KTPH004Select Last OutputKTPH005 and KTPH006Copy Last OutputKTPH007 in its right-click menu, all greyed out while a full-screen program runs, and the last two also until a command finished. A pane whose shell sends no marks shows KTPH008Set Up Shell Integration…KTPH009 instead, which opens the window with the snippets described under KTPH010Setting it upKTPH011. Neither shows while shell integration is switched off, or for a connection whose terminal emulation cannot carry the marks (Wyse, TeleVideo, HP, IBM 3270 and 5250, PETSCII).
Selecting and copying a command's outputKTPH000
KTPH000EditKTPH001 menu and the terminal's right-click menu
KTPH000EditKTPH001 menu and the terminal's right-click menu

KTPH000Select Last OutputKTPH001 selects everything the last command printed, as if you had dragged over it with the mouse: KTPH002Edit → CopyKTPH003 then copies it, and with KTPH004Copy selection to clipboard automaticallyKTPH005 in KTPH006Settings → TerminalKTPH007 it is copied at once. KTPH008Copy Last OutputKTPH009 puts the output on the clipboard straight away and leaves the selection you have as it is. Neither has a key of its own.

The output runs from the line below the command line to where the next prompt starts; the prompt and the command line are not part of it. The copy has no line break at its end, and empty lines at its end are left out. Output without a line break at its end, such as that of KTPH000, ends where the next prompt starts on the same line.

The last command is the newest one that finished. While a command such as KTPH000 still runs, both take the output of the command before it, and a prompt where you pressed KTPH002KTPH001KTPH003 without a command does not count.

KTPH000Edit → Select Last OutputKTPH001 and KTPH002Edit → Copy Last OutputKTPH003 act in the focused pane of the selected tab, the right-click menu in the pane you right-clicked. The status bar says what was selected or copied, or why nothing was: no command has finished in the pane yet, the command printed nothing, a full-screen program runs in the pane, or the shell sends no marks.

When the output is longer than the scrollback holds, its first lines are already gone: both then take what is left, from the oldest line in the scrollback, and the status bar says that the start is missing. Raise KTPH000ScrollbackKTPH001 in KTPH002Settings → TerminalKTPH003 to keep longer outputs whole.
Copies go through korTTY's clipboard, so the enterprise policy's KTPH000internal clipboard modeKTPH001 keeps them inside korTTY.

Both need the marks for the start of the output and the end of the command (OSC 133 C and D), which korTTY's snippets send. A shell set up some other way that marks only its prompts gets prompt jumps, but the status bar then says that no command has finished.

The command timestamp sidebar on the left of the terminal shows how each command the shell marked ended. The sidebar is off by default: turn it on with KTPH006View → Show Command TimestampsKTPH007 (KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH002KTPH013 on macOS, KTPH014KTPH003KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH004KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH005KTPH019 on Windows and Linux) or KTPH020Show Command TimestampsKTPH021 in the terminal's right-click menu, or for every new terminal with KTPH022Show command timestampsKTPH023 in KTPH024Settings → TerminalKTPH025. korTTY keeps the statuses while the sidebar is hidden, so turning it on shows them for the commands that already ran.
The command finished with exit status 0
The command finished with any other exit status, for example 1 for an error or 130 after KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003+KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005
The command still runs; the mark stands on the first line of its output

A finished command's mark stands on the line where it finished, which is where the shell prints the next prompt. The time on that line is when the command finished, and above it, next to the date, the command's runtime replaces the time since the previous mark: KTPH000, KTPH001, or KTPH002 for a command that took less than a second. The runtime counts from the moment the command started to the moment it finished, without the time you spent typing it.
Pointing at the line shows the date and time, the KTPH000RuntimeKTPH001 and the KTPH002Exit statusKTPH003; pointing at the … of a running command shows how long it has been running.

Without shell integration, the sidebar takes a command to be finished after half a second without new output, which marks a command that pauses before it prints more as finished too early. For a command the shell marked, korTTY waits for the shell's mark instead. Commands the shell does not mark, such as those you type into a program or into a second ssh session started from the first, keep the half-second guess.
Each mark has a shape of its own besides its colour, so you can tell them apart without telling green from red. A shell that reports no exit status shows the runtime without a mark.
While shell integration is switched off, the sidebar shows no marks and the time since the previous mark again.
The sidebar has a fixed width: with a very large terminal font, a long runtime or the mark can be cut off at its right edge.
Notification when a long command finishesKTPH000

When a command that ran at least 30 seconds finishes in a tab you are not looking at, korTTY marks the tab with 🔔 and shows a desktop notification with the tab's name, the exit status and the runtime, for example KTPH000Command failed (exit 1) after 2 min 14 sec.KTPH001 It never shows the command itself. KTPH002Settings → Terminal → NotificationsKTPH003 switches the notification off or changes the 30 seconds; see KTPH004Long-running commandsKTPH005 for the details.

Add the snippet for your shell to its startup file on every computer whose shell you want marked: on each server you connect to with SSH, and on your own computer for local shell tabs. korTTY never changes files on a server and never types anything into an SSH session to set this up. Open a new shell, or reconnect the tab, after adding the snippet.

KTPH000Set Up Shell Integration…KTPH001 opens a window with the snippets: from the right-click menu of a terminal whose shell sends no marks, or with the button of the same name in KTPH002Settings → Terminal → Shell integrationKTPH003, which works while the setting is off too. It has a tab for bash, zsh and fish, each with where the snippet goes and the snippet itself, the same text as below.

KTPH000CopyKTPH001 puts the snippet of the selected tab on the clipboard, ready to paste into the startup file in an editor on the server. Pasted at a shell prompt instead, it marks only that shell, until it exits. The copy goes through korTTY's clipboard, so with the enterprise policy's KTPH002internal clipboard modeKTPH003 the snippet stays inside korTTY, and the window says so: paste it into a korTTY terminal or editor then. You can also select part of the text and copy that.

The window opens on the shell you picked last, bash the first time. From the right-click menu of a local shell tab that runs bash, zsh or fish, it opens on that shell instead; korTTY cannot tell which shell a server runs, so for an SSH connection pick the shell yourself.

The window does not block the rest of korTTY, so it can stay open while you paste the snippet into a terminal. There is only one: opening it again brings it to the front. KTPH000Shell integration in the manualKTPH001 at its bottom opens this page.
runs only in an interactive shell whose KTPH000 is not KTPH001, so KTPH002, KTPH003 and scripts that read the startup file are not affected;
loads only once, even when the startup file is read twice;
keeps your prompt and the KTPH000, KTPH001 or event hooks you already have;
also reports the shell's working directory with OSC 7, which korTTY uses as the session's current directory, for example for relative file paths and KTPH000Open in Snippet EditorKTPH001.

To check that it works, run a few commands and press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 (KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on Windows and Linux), or right-click the terminal: KTPH018Previous PromptKTPH019 instead of KTPH020Set Up Shell Integration…KTPH021 means the marks arrive.

For bash 4.4 or later; in an older bash, such as the bash 3.2 that macOS ships as KTPH000, it does nothing. Save it on the server as KTPH001 and add KTPH002 as the last line of KTPH003, or paste it at the end of KTPH004. It has to come after anything else that sets KTPH005 or KTPH006, such as starship, oh-my-bash or liquidprompt.

For zsh 5.1 or later. Save it as KTPH000 and add KTPH001 as the last line of KTPH002, or paste it at the end of KTPH003, after oh-my-zsh, prezto or starship. With powerlevel10k, set KTPH004 in KTPH005 instead: powerlevel10k then sends the marks itself.
For fish 3.1 or later. Save it as KTPH000; fish reads that folder on its own.
KTPH000tmux and screenKTPH001 do not pass the marks on, so a shell inside them has none. Run the shell outside tmux, or set up tmux's own prompt navigation.
KTPH000MoshKTPH001 connections never carry them: mosh-server draws the screen itself and drops the marks.

KTPH001Local Windows shellsKTPH002: the snippets cover bash, zsh and fish, not KTPH000 or PowerShell, and whether Windows passes the marks of a shell such as Git Bash or WSL on depends on the Windows version.

KTPH000ResizingKTPH001: when a width change rewraps long lines, a jump can land a few lines off for prompts above the rewrapped text, the output that KTPH002Select Last OutputKTPH003 and KTPH004Copy Last OutputKTPH005 take can be off by as many lines, and so can the exit-status marks in the timestamp sidebar, like its timestamps.

KTPH000Nested sshKTPH001: OSC 7 names a host, but korTTY ignores it, so when you ssh on from the first server to a second one that also has the snippet, the second server's directory is taken for the first one's.

KTPH000Fake marksKTPH001: any program can print OSC 133 marks. The worst a fake mark does is send a jump to the wrong line, make KTPH002Select Last OutputKTPH003 and KTPH004Copy Last OutputKTPH005 take other lines of the pane than the last command's output, show a wrong exit status, runtime or finishing time in the timestamp sidebar, or mark the tab and show a KTPH006Command finishedKTPH007 notification with a made-up exit status. The notification's text is korTTY's own, so a fake mark cannot put words of its own into it, and the runtime is measured by korTTY, so at most one such notification per tab every 10 seconds is possible.

The marks and the exit statuses exist only in korTTY's memory for as long as the pane is open: they are not saved with a KTPH000projectKTPH001, a restored project's output has none, and they never leave your computer. The times commands finished are timestamps like any other, which a project saves with the sidebar's other timestamps.

KTPH001Settings → Terminal → Shell integrationKTPH002 has KTPH003Use the command marks of shells set up for shell integration (OSC 133)KTPH004, on by default. Switched off, korTTY ignores the marks: the prompt keys reach the program, the right-click menu shows no shell-integration entries, the timestamp sidebar shows no exit statuses, no long command marks its tab or notifies, and korTTY tells that an SSH session is at its prompt from the prompt's text alone, for the AI Agent's KTPH000 commands and for the question before closing a busy tab. This one setting covers every use of the marks; KTPH005Settings → AIKTPH006 no longer has an option of its own for them. The change applies to open tabs as soon as you save. The marks stay invisible either way, because the terminal never shows OSC 133 sequences. See KTPH007Terminal settingsKTPH008.
